title: Minimum-SLA-Drift Upgrade Controller for Dedicated GPU Fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a rollout controller that upgrades dedicated GPU pools with an explicit SLA-drift budget. The controller should coordinate with the autoscaler to reserve transient capacity, perform soft-drain (evict low-priority slices first), and shape traffic to keep 99th-p50 latency delta under a configurable threshold during upgrades. Integrates with LTS channel gating so only approved LTS builds are eligible for traffic promotion.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controller can schedule an upgrade wave against a specified GPU pool and hold measurable capacity hedges; 2) During rollout, observed 99p latency delta vs baseline remains <= configured budget in 95% of synthetic and tenant canaries; 3) Automatic rollback triggers on sustained SLO violation for >5 minutes and executes fast-path capacity reallocation; 4) Console shows per-wave metrics (capacity reserved, evicted tenants, latency delta, rollback events); 5) Documented runbook and one successful dry-run on staging fleet.
technical_design: - New UpgradeController CRD (controller logic implemented in k8s operator) that computes wave size by utilization histogram matching; - Autoscaler handshake API: UpgradeController requests "capacity hedges" with eviction predicates and TTL; - Soft-drain strategy: evict preemptible/low-priority slices first, apply rate-limited eviction and a backoff when error budget is low; - Canary selection: pick tenants from three utility buckets (low-latency, bulk-embed, high-throughput) to validate representative load. - LTS gating: controller checks release metadata store for channel=stable/lts before promoting; - Telemetry: emit rollout_id, wave_index, reserved_units, eviction_count, observed_latency_p50/p95/p99, and rollback_reason.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind 'min-sla-drift' for internal pilots; 2) Canary on staging fleet with synthetic traffic generators (step load, pathing, embeddings) week 1; 3) Dry-run on a low-util production pool (night window) week 2; 4) Phased waves across remaining pools with 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% promotion, 1h observation per wave; 5) If rollback triggers, runbook executes capacity re-add and cancels remaining waves.
test_plan: - Unit tests for controller decision logic and autoscaler handshake; - Integration tests with autoscaler simulator (fault-injection: delayed capacity, failed evictions); - End-to-end on staging with synthetic tenant profiles; - Load soak test for 6 hours to verify no long-tail regressions; - Chaos test: intermittent node terminations during waves to ensure graceful handling.
risks: - Under-reserving capacity leads to customer tail latency spikes; - Over-reserving reduces throughput and increases cost for Dedicated customers; - Incorrect tenant prioritization could evict critical workloads; - Autoscaler API contract changes may break handshake; - Observability gaps could delay rollback decisions.
